per_qid_evidence.expected_sql_shape: WITH cohort AS (...) SELECT cohort_month, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM cohort c1 JOIN cohort c2 ON c1.customer_id = c2.customer_id AND c2.cohort_month > c1.cohort_month

result.intent_description: Teach Genie the cohort-retention self-join pattern: CTE to define cohort, then JOIN cohort to itself on customer_id with a later event_month to count returning customers. Pattern is not in the closed catalog (OTHER).
result.rationale: Cluster's expected_sql_shape uses a self-join that no closed repair_shape captures; OTHER + add_example_sql teaches the structure once.

patch_body.example_question: Of the customers who first appeared in January, how many returned in February?
patch_body.example_sql: WITH cohort AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(event_month) AS cohort_month FROM analytics.customer_events GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT c1.cohort_month, COUNT(DISTINCT c2.customer_id) AS returning_customers FROM cohort c1 JOIN cohort c2 ON c1.customer_id = c2.customer_id WHERE c2.cohort_month > c1.cohort_month GROUP BY c1.cohort_month
patch_body.usage_guidance: Use when the user asks about cohort retention or follow-on activity.
